/-!
# Conjecture 9.13

by D. I. Zaitsev

Is a soluble torsion-free group minimax if it satisfies the weak minimum condition
for normal subgroups?

Here a group is *minimax* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$
each of whose factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ satisfies the maximal condition (Max) or the
minimal condition (Min) on subgroups. A group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimum condition
for normal subgroups* if for every descending chain $N_0 \geq N_1 \geq \dots$ of normal
subgroups of $G$ the index $|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ is finite for all but finitely many $i$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
For subgroups $H \leq K$ of $G$, the pair $(H, K)$ is a *Max-or-Min step* if $H$ is normal
in $K$ and the factor group $K/H$ satisfies the maximal condition on subgroups (every ascending
chain of subgroups is finite) or the minimal condition on subgroups (every descending chain of
subgroups is finite).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `RelSeries`/`CompositionSeries` (no group/factor-condition support), `derivedSeries` (specific to solvability), `WellFoundedGT`/`WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)` (used as the Max/Min conditions).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.13».IsMaxOrMinStep
justification.why_needed: Auxiliary predicate for one step of a subnormal series: `H ≤ K`, `H` normal in `K`, and the factor `K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K` satisfies Max (`WellFoundedGT (Subgroup _)`) or Min (`WellFoundedLT (Subgroup _)`). Mathlib has no notion of a subnormal series with factor conditions.

blocks.name: IsMaxOrMinStep
blocks.text:
/-- For subgroups $H \leq K$ of $G$, the pair $(H, K)$ is a *Max-or-Min step* if $H$ is normal
in $K$ and the factor group $K/H$ satisfies the maximal condition on subgroups (every ascending
chain of subgroups is finite) or the minimal condition on subgroups (every descending chain of
subgroups is finite). -/
def IsMaxOrMinStep (H K : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  H ≤ K ∧ ∃ _ : (H.subgroupOf K).Normal,
    WellFoundedGT (Subgroup (K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K)) ∨
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup (K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K))

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *minimax* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ each of whose
factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ satisfies the maximal condition or the minimal condition on subgroups.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable`, `Group.IsNilpotent` (analogous finite-series notions, but with different factor conditions); nothing for minimax.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.13».IsMinimax
justification.why_needed: 'Minimax group' (finite subnormal series `⊥ = s 0 ≤ … ≤ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤` each of whose factors satisfies Max or Min) is not in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

blocks.name: IsMinimax
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *minimax* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ each of whose
factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ satisfies the maximal condition or the minimal condition on subgroups. -/
def IsMinimax (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, IsMaxOrMinStep (s i.castSucc) (s i.succ)

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimum condition for normal subgroups* if for every
descending chain $N_0 \geq N_1 \geq N_2 \geq \dots$ of normal subgroups of $G$, the index
$|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ is finite for all but finitely many $i$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)` (the ordinary Min condition, too strong), `Subgroup.IsFiniteRelIndex` (used for the finite-index part).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.13».WeakMinNormal
justification.why_needed: Zaitsev's weak minimal condition on normal subgroups (for every descending chain `N : ℕ → Subgroup G` of normal subgroups, `|N i : N (i+1)|` is finite for all but finitely many `i`) is not in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: WeakMinNormal
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimum condition for normal subgroups* if for every
descending chain $N_0 \geq N_1 \geq N_2 \geq \dots$ of normal subgroups of $G$, the index
$|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ is finite for all but finitely many $i$. -/
def WeakMinNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ N : ℕ → Subgroup G, (∀ i, (N i).Normal) → Antitone N →
    {i : ℕ | ¬ (N (i + 1)).IsFiniteRelIndex (N i)}.Finite

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMinimax_of_wellFoundedGT [WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G)] : IsMinimax G := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => ?_⟩
  rw [Fin.fin_one_eq_zero i]
  show IsMaxOrMinStep ⊥ ⊤
  haveI : ((⊥ : Subgroup G).subgroupOf ⊤).Normal := by
    rw [Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]; infer_instance
  let e : ((⊤ : Subgroup G) ⧸ (⊥ : Subgroup G).subgroupOf ⊤) ≃* G :=
    ((QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq (Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf ⊤)).trans
      QuotientGroup.quotientBot).trans Subgroup.topEquiv
  exact ⟨bot_le, this, Or.inl (MulEquiv.mapSubgroup e).toOrderEmbedding.wellFoundedGT⟩

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem weakMinNormal_of_wellFoundedLT [WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)] : WeakMinNormal G := by
  intro N _ hN
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := WellFoundedGT.monotone_chain_condition
    (⟨OrderDual.toDual ∘ N, fun _ _ h => hN h⟩ : ℕ →o (Subgroup G)ᵒᵈ)
  refine (Set.finite_Iio k).subset fun i hi => ?_
  by_contra hik
  rw [Set.mem_Iio, not_lt] at hik
  refine hi ⟨?_⟩
  have h₁ : N k = N (i + 1) := hk _ (by omega)
  have h₂ : N k = N i := hk _ (by omega)
  rw [← h₁, ← h₂, Subgroup.relIndex_self]
  exact one_ne_zero

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question with an implicit universal quantifier over groups: the Prop is 'every soluble (solvable) torsion-free group satisfying the weak minimal condition on normal subgroups (Min-n-∞: every descending chain of normal subgroups has all but finitely many indices finite) is minimax (has a finite subnormal series each of whose factors satisfies Max or Min)'; note 'soluble' = solvable, and 'minimax' and 'weak minimum condition' are not in Mathlib and must be defined explicitly.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 states the question faithfully: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [IsSolvable G], (∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1) → WeakMinNormal G → IsMinimax G. Torsion-free is encoded as 'only the identity has finite order' (the standard notion for arbitrary groups). WeakMinNormal quantifies over ℕ-indexed antitone chains of normal subgroups and requires |N_i : N_{i+1}| finite for all but finitely many i (IsFiniteRelIndex = relIndex ≠ 0; relIndex is 0 exactly for infinite index). IsMinimax is a finite series ⊥ = s₀ ≤ … ≤ sₙ = ⊤ with each term normal in the next and each factor group (a genuine quotient, with the Group instance coming from the existentially bound Normal witness — verified via #print) satisfying WellFoundedGT (Max) or WellFoundedLT (Min) on its subgroup lattice. It compiles with only the sorry warning, follows the Kourovka/1_40 file style, and includes three proved sanity lemmas. c01 and c07 are mathematically equivalent alternatives; c04 was chosen for the cleanest structure (explicit H ≤ K in IsMaxOrMinStep) and documentation. c02, c03, c05, c06, c08 were rejected because they encode torsion-free as Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree (injectivity of x ↦ xⁿ for all n ≠ 0, i.e. unique roots), whose equivalence with 'no nontrivial element of finite order' is only proved for CommGroup and is genuinely strictly stronger for non-abelian groups (e.g. the torsion-free polycyclic Klein bottle group ⟨a,b | aba⁻¹ = b⁻¹⟩ has (ab)² = a² with ab ≠ a); this would quantify over a strictly smaller class of groups than Zaitsev's question.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.13

by D. I. Zaitsev

Is a soluble torsion-free group minimax if it satisfies the weak minimum condition
for normal subgroups?

Here a group is *minimax* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$
each of whose factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ satisfies the maximal condition (Max) or the
minimal condition (Min) on subgroups. A group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimum condition
for normal subgroups* if for every descending chain $N_0 \geq N_1 \geq \dots$ of normal
subgroups of $G$ the index $|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ is finite for all but finitely many $i$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.13»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- For subgroups $H \leq K$ of $G$, the pair $(H, K)$ is a *Max-or-Min step* if $H$ is normal
in $K$ and the factor group $K/H$ satisfies the maximal condition on subgroups (every ascending
chain of subgroups is finite) or the minimal condition on subgroups (every descending chain of
subgroups is finite). -/
def IsMaxOrMinStep (H K : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  H ≤ K ∧ ∃ _ : (H.subgroupOf K).Normal,
    WellFoundedGT (Subgroup (K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K)) ∨
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup (K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K))

/-- A group $G$ is *minimax* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ each of whose
factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ satisfies the maximal condition or the minimal condition on subgroups. -/
def IsMinimax (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, IsMaxOrMinStep (s i.castSucc) (s i.succ)

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the *weak minimum condition for normal subgroups* if for every
descending chain $N_0 \geq N_1 \geq N_2 \geq \dots$ of normal subgroups of $G$, the index
$|N_i : N_{i+1}|$ is finite for all but finitely many $i$. -/
def WeakMinNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ N : ℕ → Subgroup G, (∀ i, (N i).Normal) → Antitone N →
    {i : ℕ | ¬ (N (i + 1)).IsFiniteRelIndex (N i)}.Finite

/-- The trivial group is minimax. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMinimax_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton G] : IsMinimax G :=
  ⟨0, fun _ => ⊥, rfl, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- A group satisfying the maximal condition on subgroups is minimax. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMinimax_of_wellFoundedGT [WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G)] : IsMinimax G := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => ?_⟩
  rw [Fin.fin_one_eq_zero i]
  show IsMaxOrMinStep ⊥ ⊤
  haveI : ((⊥ : Subgroup G).subgroupOf ⊤).Normal := by
    rw [Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]; infer_instance
  let e : ((⊤ : Subgroup G) ⧸ (⊥ : Subgroup G).subgroupOf ⊤) ≃* G :=
    ((QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq (Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf ⊤)).trans
      QuotientGroup.quotientBot).trans Subgroup.topEquiv
  exact ⟨bot_le, this, Or.inl (MulEquiv.mapSubgroup e).toOrderEmbedding.wellFoundedGT⟩

/-- A group satisfying the minimal condition on subgroups satisfies the weak minimum condition
for normal subgroups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem weakMinNormal_of_wellFoundedLT [WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)] : WeakMinNormal G := by
  intro N _ hN
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := WellFoundedGT.monotone_chain_condition
    (⟨OrderDual.toDual ∘ N, fun _ _ h => hN h⟩ : ℕ →o (Subgroup G)ᵒᵈ)
  refine (Set.finite_Iio k).subset fun i hi => ?_
  by_contra hik
  rw [Set.mem_Iio, not_lt] at hik
  refine hi ⟨?_⟩
  have h₁ : N k = N (i + 1) := hk _ (by omega)
  have h₂ : N k = N i := hk _ (by omega)
  rw [← h₁, ← h₂, Subgroup.relIndex_self]
  exact one_ne_zero

/--
Is a soluble torsion-free group minimax if it satisfies the weak minimum condition for normal
subgroups?

That is, is every soluble torsion-free group satisfying the weak minimum condition for normal
subgroups a minimax group? Here torsion-free means that the identity is the only element of
finite order.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.13» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [IsSolvable G],
      (∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1) → WeakMinNormal G → IsMinimax G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.13»

items: Torsion-free is stated as `∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1` rather than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree G`. The latter means `x ↦ x^n` is injective for all `n ≠ 0`, which for non-abelian groups is strictly stronger than 'no non-trivial element of finite order' (Mathlib's `isMulTorsionFree_iff_not_isOfFinOrder` needs `CommGroup`); e.g. the torsion-free metabelian Klein bottle group `⟨a,b | aba⁻¹ = b⁻¹⟩` has `(ab)² = a²`, so `IsMulTorsionFree` would wrongly exclude typical torsion-free soluble groups. (Note: `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Kaplansky.lean` uses `IsMulTorsionFree` for 'torsion-free group'; that may deserve a look, but it is out of scope here.)

'Minimax' uses a finite *subnormal* series (each term normal in the next), following Robinson / Lennox–Robinson and the decomposition notes. This matters: e.g. `ℤ[1/p] ⋊ ℤ` is a torsion-free soluble minimax group under this (standard) definition but has no finite series of subgroups *normal in G* with Max-or-Min factors.

Factors `K/H` are modelled as `↥K ⧸ H.subgroupOf K` with the normality hypothesis supplied via `∃ _ : (H.subgroupOf K).Normal, …` (a Prop, so no instance-mismatch issues). Max/Min are `WellFoundedGT`/`WellFoundedLT` on `Subgroup (K ⧸ …)`, matching Mathlib's own usage of `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)` for the minimal condition in `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Solvable.lean`.

The weak minimal condition quantifies over ℕ-indexed antitone chains of normal subgroups (non-strict chains are allowed; repeats have index 1, so this is equivalent to the strictly-descending formulation) and requires `{i | ¬ (N (i+1)).IsFiniteRelIndex (N i)}` to be finite, i.e. `|N i : N (i+1)|` finite for all but finitely many `i`. `(N (i+1)).IsFiniteRelIndex (N i)` is finiteness of the index of `N (i+1) ⊓ N i = N (i+1)` in `N i`.
The group is quantified at universe `Type`, as in the other Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76). `answer(True)` asserts every such group is minimax; `answer(False)` asserts a counterexample exists.

Three `category test` lemmas check the definitions are not degenerate: the trivial group is minimax, any group with Max (e.g. ℤ) is minimax, and any group with Min satisfies the weak minimal condition on normal subgroups.

reviewer_notes: Final file is c04's candidate.lean unchanged (compiled: only 'declaration uses sorry'). Key adjudication point: 'torsion-free' must be 'no nontrivial element of finite order', not Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree (unique-roots / R-group condition), which is strictly stronger for non-abelian groups; Mathlib no longer has Monoid.IsTorsionFree, so the explicit ∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1 is used. Note that FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Kaplansky.lean uses IsMulTorsionFree for 'torsion-free group' — that may deserve review by maintainers but is out of scope here. Minimax uses a subnormal series (each term normal in the next), the standard Baer/Robinson/Zaitsev definition; a normal-series variant would be inequivalent (e.g. Z[1/p] ⋊ Z). Weak Min-n is stated for non-strict ℕ-indexed descending chains, equivalent to the strict formulation since repeated terms have index 1. The bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean) rather than FormalConjecturesForMathlib, since the task requires a single final file; maintainers may wish to move IsMinimax / WeakMinNormal to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as reusable definitions. Groups are quantified over Type (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files.
